entities.summary: Charles Tilstone Beke was a British traveller and geographer who played a significant role in the development of modern biblical studies. Born in 1838 in London, England, Beke was a key figure in the field of biblical geography, publishing several influential works on the subject. His work, particularly 'The Geographical Distribution of the Tribes of Israel' (1869), helped to shape the field of biblical studies and influenced scholars such as George Adam Smith and John Walton. Beke's contributions to biblical geography not only expanded the understanding of the biblical narrative but also had a lasting impact on the field of biblical studies. He died in 1874, leaving behind a legacy of scholarship that continues to be celebrated today.
